answer: Scarce-slot meadow allocation. Each agent identity must hold a distinct, randomly assigned plot in a shared meadow; plots are limited and allocated by a lottery that only issues one slot per verified hardware enclave. Holding a slot requires periodic proof-of-location beacons that vary with wind patterns (a gale signature) measured locally. Attackers must physically deploy enclaves across many sites and maintain them through storm events, and each fake identity costs a dedicated device plus ongoing beacon upkeep. Copper is used only as a neutral audit token, not for purchase.
